findings.title: Queries are now interpolated twice (ad hoc filters applied twice)
findings.body: `runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on every target, but the sub-requests it builds (`{ ...request, targets }`) still carry the original `scopedVars`/`filters` and are executed through `datasource.runQuery()` -> `DataSourceWithBackend.query()`, which calls `applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` again for each target. The result is that interpolation runs twice on the same query: (a) `addAdHocFilters` is applied a second time to an expression that already contains those matchers, so ad hoc/adhoc-variable label matchers end up duplicated in the LogQL sent to Loki (e.g. `{app="x", env="prod", env="prod"}`), and (b) `templateSrv.replace` is re-run over a string that already contains substituted variable values, so any value that itself contains `$name`/`${name}` is expanded a second time, silently changing the query. Either strip `scopedVars`/`filters` from the sub-request, or flag the request as already interpolated so the downstream call is skipped.

findings.title: Shard splitting path interpolates each query three times
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates the targets with `applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)`, then hands the resulting sub-request (which still contains `scopedVars` and `filters`) to `runSplitQuery`, which interpolates again (querySplitting.ts:299), and finally `datasource.runQuery` -> `DataSourceWithBackend.query` interpolates a third time. The new assertion `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` in shardQuerySplitting.test.ts confirms the repeated calls (1 up-front + 1 per sub-request). Beyond wasted work (each call re-parses the LogQL expression in `addAdHocFilters`), repeated application of ad hoc filters duplicates label matchers and repeated `templateSrv.replace` can re-expand `$`-containing variable values in the already-interpolated expression, including the injected `__stream_shard__` selector context. Interpolation should happen exactly once per query.

findings.title: Assertion locks in redundant interpolation count
findings.body: `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` asserts that a single target is interpolated five times (once in `runShardSplitQuery` plus once per shard sub-request inside `runSplitQuery`). This encodes the redundant re-interpolation as expected behaviour, so a future fix that interpolates only once will fail this test, and the test is coupled to the number of shard groups rather than to the thing being verified (that queries are interpolated before being run). Prefer asserting that the targets reaching `runQuery` are interpolated, or `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` once the duplicate interpolation is removed. Note also that the mock mutates `query.expr` in place and is only correct because the substitution happens to be idempotent.

findings.title: New test does not cover the actual regression (step used for partitioning)
findings.body: The bug being fixed is that an un-interpolated `step` (e.g. `step: '$step'`) does not match the interval regex in `calculateStep`, so the metric time-range partitioning falls back to `intervalMs` and produces wrong split boundaries. The new test only asserts that `targets[0].expr`/`targets[0].step` on the first `runQuery` call are interpolated; it never asserts that the partitions/ranges (or the number of sub-requests) now reflect the interpolated step. The existing 'Correctly splits queries with step' test shows how range boundaries differ by step, so the fix could regress (e.g. interpolation moved back after partitioning) while this test still passes.

findings.title: Test's replace mock ignores scopedVars, so `$__auto` substitution is unrealistic
findings.body: The test's `replace: (input = '') => input.replace('$__auto', '5m')...` ignores the `scopedVars` argument. The real Loki `applyTemplateVariables` deliberately passes macros such as `$__auto`, `$__interval` and `$__range` through by overriding them in the scopedVars it hands to `templateSrv.replace`, so in production `count_over_time({a="b"}[$__auto])` is left untouched on the frontend and interpolated on the backend. The test therefore asserts a substitution that cannot happen in the real data source and gives false confidence about macro handling. Using a user-defined variable (e.g. `$range`/`$step`) would exercise the same code path realistically.
